{{Quote|Today, I'm excited to share with you that Jon and Dave are concurrently developing two new spinoff series exclusively for Disney+: one, The Rangers of the New Republic, and the other featuring fan-favorite Ahsoka Tano. Set within the timeline of The Mandalorian, these interconnected shows, along with future stories, will excite new audiences, embrace our most passionate fans, and will culminate in a climactic story event.|President Kathleen Kennedy announces ''Ahsoka'' during Disney Investor Day 2020|<ref name="Disney Investor">{{DisneyCompany|url=disney-investor-day-2020|text=Disney Investor Day 2020}}</ref>}}
'''''Star Wars: Ahsoka''''' is a live-action television series that was first announced on [[December 10]], [[2020]]. Its [[Ahsoka Season 1|first season]] streamed exclusively on [[Disney+]] in [[2023]]. It is written by [[Dave Filoni]] and produced by him and [[Jon Favreau]] and stars [[Rosario Dawson]] as [[Ahsoka Tano]]. It is set in [[9 ABY]] after Ahsoka Tano's appearance in ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian|The Mandalorian]]'' [[The Mandalorian Season Two|season two]] and follows her search for [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]] started in the epilogue of the animated series ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]''. A [[Ahsoka Season 2|second season]] was announced on [[January 9]], [[2024]] and the series' story will be concluded by an [[Untitled Star Wars film (Dave Filoni)|upcoming untitled film]] directed by Filoni.

==Official description==
''Set after the fall of the Empire, ''Ahsoka'' follows the former Jedi knight Ahsoka Tano as she investigates an emerging threat to a vulnerable galaxy.''<ref name="D23 showcase">{{D23|url=magical-moments-from-studio-showcase-day-2-marvel-studios-lucasfilm-and-20th-century-studios|text=All the Magic from Studio Showcase, Day 2: Marvel Studios, Lucasfilm, and 20th Century Studios}}</ref>

==Development==
{{Quote|Ahsoka'' is a continuous story. It is definitely driving toward a goal, in my mind, as opposed to being little singular adventures. That's what I want the character to be doing, and I think that's what fans want now. They have such a relationship with her. I've only recently started to understand that all those kids that watched Clone Wars are now a lot older—they're very excited about all the things they grew up with, as they should be.''|italics=0|Dave Filoni|<ref name="Vanity Fair">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/05/star-wars-cover-the-rebellion-will-be-televised|text='Star Wars': The Rebellion Will Be Televised|author=Anthony Breznican|date=2022-05-17|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']]|archivedate=20220517114556}}</ref>}}
[[File:Ahsoka_D23.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Jon Favreau, Dave Filoni, and Kathleen Kennedy presenting a production still from ''Ahsoka'' at D23 Expo 2022]]
Rumors of a live-action [[Ahsoka Tano]]–led series first circulated on the internet back in [[March]] of [[2020]],<ref name="Manabyte">{{WebCite|url=http://manabyte.com/2020/03/rumor-live-action-ahsoka-tano-series-being-planned-in-very-early-development|text=Rumor: Live Action Ahsoka Tano Series Being Planned, in Very Early Development|author=Jeremy Conrad|date=2020-03-30|work=[http://manabyte.com ManaByte]|archivedate=20210127170553}}</ref> just weeks after [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney]] CEO Bob Iger hinted at an earnings call that spinoffs of characters from ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'' were in development.<ref name="The HR">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/disneys-bob-iger-teases-mandalorian-falcon-winter-soldier-wandavision-dates-1276326|text=Disney's Bob Iger Considering 'Mandalorian' Spinoff Shows|author=Aaron Couch|date=2020-01-04|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20210127171046}}</ref> When Tano made her live-action debut in "[[Chapter 13: The Jedi]]" in [[The Mandalorian Season Two|''The Mandalorian'' Season Two]], she became a character that could be the focus of a ''Mandalorian'' spin-off,<ref name="Chapter 13">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 13: The Jedi}}</ref> and the series was officially announced by [[Lucasfilm]] President [[Kathleen Kennedy]] on an investors day presentation on [[December 10]], 2020. A [[StarWars.com]] post later that day confirmed that [[Jon Favreau]] and [[Dave Filoni]] would executive produce the series, and that it would be written by Filoni and star [[Rosario Dawson]].<ref name="Announcement" />

On [[October 22]], [[2021]], Rosario Dawson announced on [[Wikipedia:Instagram|Instagram]] that [[Hayden Christensen]] would reprise his role as [[Anakin Skywalker]] in ''Ahsoka''. However, the post was later taken down.<ref name="Instagram">{{Instagram|username=rosariodawson|url=p/CVWTh3nvmsh|name=[[Rosario Dawson]]|quote=Skyguy, …They know!!! See you soon, Snips|archivefile=File:DawsonInstagram.jpg|nolive=1}}</ref>

On [[May 9]], [[2022]], the show started production<ref name="SW Production tweet">{{Twitter|starwars|status/1523694289770868737|[[Star Wars]]|quote=Ahsoka, an Original series, starts production today.|archivedate=20220509162150}}</ref> under the name "Stormcrow."<ref name="Stormcrow">{{OfficialYouTube|channel=@Comicbook|name=Comicbook.com|video=JiaIS02mHfY|text=The Legacy of Huyang – Star Wars: Ahsoka Featurette|''ComicBook.com''}}|date=2024-11-26|archivedate=20241205095545}}</ref> The creator of [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo]] "Thrawn," [[Timothy Zahn]], was consulted, and will continue to be consulted with, for matters concerning the Grand Admiral's character<ref name="Ahsoka Zahn tweet 1">{{Twitter|empiremagazine|status/1644660148198055940|Empire Magazine|quote=Dave Filoni says they have spoken – and are continuing to speak – with Timothy Zahn about Thrawn's character. “That all starts with Tim Zahn's books,” he says. “When we were all kids, hungry for something else, and Heir To The Empire hit,” he remembers, “it was so unique and so wonderful.” Thrawn is not to be messed with. “He doesn't have the Force, but it doesn't matter. He will outsmart you,” says Filoni. #StarWarsCelebration|archivedate=20230408124058}}</ref> to make sure Thrawn was written just right.<ref name="Ahsoka Zahn tweet 2">{{Twitter|username=sw_holocron|url=status/1644658007383461894|name=Star Wars Holocron|quote=Dave Filoni consulted with Timothy Zahn on how to bring Grand Admiral Thrawn to life in the Ahsoka series. “We want to make sure we get it right.” #StarWars #StarWarsCelebration #StarWarsCelebration2023|archivedate=20230408122554}}</ref> Zahn himself said he had "spoken a couple of times" about Thrawn and would "discuss things more thoroughly in the future."<ref name="Zahn interview clip">{{Twitter|username=PocketImaginair|url=status/1649393837738000385|name=Pocket Imaginaire|quote=On a profité de la venue de Timothy Zahn au @ParisFanFest pour lui poser quelques questions. L'interview complète arrive bientôt mais, en attendant, on ne pouvait pas ne pas partager cet extrait avec vous. Il concerne le devenir d'un certain grand amiral sur écrans... 😋|archivedate=20230503155857}}</ref>

On [[January 9]], [[2024]], a StarWars.com announcement of the film [[Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu|''The Mandalorian and Grogu'']] revealed that a [[Ahsoka Season 2|second season]] of ''Ahsoka'' was being developed by Dave Filoni.<ref name="The Mandalorian & Grogu">{{SW|url=news/the-mandalorian-and-grogu|text=''The Mandalorian & Grogu'' Journeys to the Big Screen}}</ref> The [[January 10|next day]], a formal announcement of ''Ahsoka'' season 2 was published to the website, including a sketch from Filoni depicting Ahsoka Tano and [[Sabine Wren]] standing on a [[Monument to the Ones|statue]] featured in the finale of Season 1 with the caption "The story continues…."<ref name="Ahsoka Season 2 article">{{SW|url=news/ahsoka-season-2-dave-filoni-sketch|text=''Ahsoka'' Season 2 in Development, New Sketch Revealed}}</ref>

==Release and reception==
At the [[Wikipedia:76th Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards|76th Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards]], held on [[September 7]] and [[September 8|8]], 2024, ''Ahsoka'' won the award for [[Wikipedia:Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Fantasy/Sci-Fi Costumes|Outstanding Fantasy/Sci-Fi Costumes]] for "[[Part Eight: The Jedi, the Witch, and the Warlord]]." The show was nominated for, but did not win, [[Wikipedia:Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Special Visual Effects|Outstanding Special Visual Effects in a Season or a Movie]], [[Wikipedia:Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Hairstyling|Outstanding Period or Fantasy/Sci-Fi Hairstyling]] (for "[[Part One: Master and Apprentice]]"), [[Wikipedia:Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Prosthetic Makeup|Outstanding Prosthetic Makeup]] (for "Part Eight: The Jedi, the Witch, and the Warlord"), and [[Wikipedia:Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Sound Editing for a Comedy or Drama Series (Half-Hour) and Animation|Outstanding Sound Editing for a Comedy or Drama Series (Half-Hour) and Animation]] (for "[[Part Four: Fallen Jedi]]," for which [[Matthew Wood]] and [[David Acord]] were included in the nomination).<ref name="EW">{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/2024-creative-arts-emmys-winners-list-8707410|text=2024 Creative Arts Emmys winners: ''Shōgun'' breaks Emmy record, ''The Bear, SNL'' win big|author=Ryan Coleman and Jillian Sederholm|date=2024-09-08|work=[[Wikipedia:Entertainment Weekly|''Entertainment Weekly'']]|archivedate=20240913225313}}</ref>
